![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14146545/assets/a84a1501854f6efb988b7c02c3a1b5a80b80dbf3d5fc7ce94406778cc6dcadb5.png)

Find the differential equation governing the amount of current $I$ (in amperes) at time $t$ (in seconds) in the circuit given in the diagram above.
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows a series RL circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of $E(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,\text{V},$ a resistor with resistance $10\,Ω,$ and an inductor with an inductance of $2\,\text{H}.$

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RL circuit, there are two voltage drops:

- The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality $R=10\,Ω.$

$$
{V}_{R}=10I
$$

- The voltage drop across the inductor is proportional to the rate of change of current, with a constant of proportionality $L=2\,\text{H}.$

$$
{V}_{L}=2\,\frac{dI}{dt}
$$

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, the differential equation governing the amount of current $I$ in the circuit is

$$
5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)=10I+2\,\frac{dI}{dt},
$$

which gives

$$
\frac{dI}{dt}+5I=\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t).
$$
